newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S&P assigns SKF note issue a BBB rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns SKF note issue a BBB rating.

text.p: U.S. credit rating agency Standard & Poor's (S&P) said on Wednesday it had assigned Swedish rollerbearings maker SKF a BBB rating for a $200 million issue of senior unsecured notes.
At the same time S&P affirmed SKF's BBB corporate credit and senior unsecured ratings.
"The longterm outlook is positive," S&P said in a statement.
"The ratings reflect SKF AB's strong position in the competitive and cyclical global bearing industry."
The agency said improvements in the company's capital structure, together with higher profit margins owing to SKF's restructuring programme, could result in a higher rating.
During recent years SKF has initiated a number of structural activities to increase productivity, lower the break-even point and increase earnings capacity.
These changes led to a sharp increase in income before depreciation between 1993 and 1995, from 1.8 billion crowns to 5.2 billion crowns.
